exposure: Implementation of a smart intrapartum surveillance system
implementation of a smart intrapartum surveillance system
cohort: 3648 women admitted for delivery, with data analyzed for 1760 deliveries before and 1888 deliveries after implementation of the surveillance system
finding: Implementation of a smart intrapartum surveillance system was associated with a significant 24.7% reduction in cesarean section rate for nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex pregnancies.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in perinatal outcomes between vaginal and cesarean birth groups before and after the implementation of the smart intrapartum surveillance system.
